metaDesc: The dessert cafes and bakeries locals actually go to in Korat (Nakhon Ratchasima), Thailand — homemade cakes, bingsu, matcha and Basque cheesecake, with areas, rough prices and opening hours.

ogTitle: Dessert Cafes & Bakeries in Korat — 10 Spots Locals Actually Go To
ogDesc: Homemade cakes, bingsu, matcha and Basque cheesecake — Korat dessert cafes that are genuinely open, with areas and prices.
intro: Korat is known for pad mee and Isan food, but the city centre is also packed with dessert cafes and bakeries that bake fresh every day — from homemade cakes in old shophouses to giant cups of bingsu, plus the Basque cheesecake and matcha that dessert fans chase down. We picked only places that are genuinely open right now and that Korat locals actually sit in, and we tell you the area, rough prices and opening hours.

blocks.html: If you're walking around central Korat and want somewhere to sit and refuel on something sweet, there's more choice than you'd think. Most places cluster in the old town around Suranari, Chomsurangyat, Chumphon and Mittraphap roads — a few minutes apart by car or Grab. We've split them into three groups: dessert cafes known for cakes and drinks, bakeries that bake fresh and sell by the piece, and cold sweet shops to beat the heat.

blocks.text: 10 dessert cafes & bakeries in central Korat

blocks.html: Ordered roughly by how often people talk about them and how solid the reviews are. Each place has its own character — see which one fits your mood.

items.name: De Forest Cafe & Bakery
items.blurb: One of the first dessert cafes that comes to mind for Korat locals. Known for big cups of bingsu and a range of cakes — when mango season hits, the fresh mango kakigori draws a very long queue. Roomy and comfy, good for groups.

items.name: Faifo Oldtown Cafe & Floral
items.blurb: A cafe in an old shophouse in the heart of the old town on Chumphon Road, decked out in a vintage-and-flowers style that photographs beautifully. The standout menu items are the matcha croissant and the strawberry-cheese cruffin.

items.name: KASEM Coffee
items.blurb: A coffee-and-homemade-cake spot that dessert lovers trust — banana cake, burnt cheesecake, orange cake, and caramel coffee with nuts. A relaxed daytime place that doesn't get too crowded.
items.meta: Det Udom Road, old town · open 08:30–17:30 (Sat–Sun 09:00–18:00)

items.name: Rosie.nak
items.blurb: Matcha fans, this is your stop. Decorated in clean whites, with a full green-tea lineup spanning drinks, bakery and ice cream. The signature is the matcha banoffee — if you like your green tea strong, you'll be happy here.

items.name: Na Bueng Coffee
items.blurb: A cafe by the Bueng Ta Lua water park where you can sit in the breeze all day. Known for its Basque cheesecake and blueberry cheesecake, with bakery, drinks and savoury dishes too. Good for bringing the family for a long sit.
items.meta: Bueng Ta Lua water park · open 09:00–18:30

items.name: La-Moon Cafe
items.blurb: A leafy cafe on Suranari Road that feels like sitting in someone's back garden, with easy-on-the-wallet prices. The standouts are the fresh-milk green tea and the blueberry cheesecake — a handy stop mid-stroll around town.

items.name: Vera Cafe & Gallery
items.blurb: A small gallery cafe where the cakes are the star — red velvet, banoffee pie and cheesecake, with friendly starting prices. Good for anyone who likes to sit quietly with a coffee and a favourite slice.

items.name: Sweet Days (Sueb Siri)
items.blurb: A garden dessert spot in the Sueb Siri area. The hits are big cups of bingsu, honey toast, and chocolate lava cake, at easygoing prices. It's been a long-time favourite with Korat's younger crowd.

items.name: So Far So Good
items.blurb: A dessert shop across from the big market, famous for a chocolate sphere that melts when hot sauce is poured over it — you'll want to film it. There's ice cream and toast too, and it's a sweet little corner most people haven't found yet.
items.meta: Opposite the big market, old town

items.name: Baan Khanom Thai (Soi Chan area)
items.blurb: For genuinely traditional Thai sweets, this place makes old-style desserts, sticky-rice snacks and coconut cake at very low prices — great to take home or as a light gift to bring back.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.html: Homemade cakes at the popular spots are often made in limited batches and sell out before evening. If you want a signature like the Basque cheesecake or mango kakigori, go in the early afternoon when the selection is fuller.

blocks.text: Fresh bakeries you can take away

blocks.html: If you'd rather not sit in and just want to grab bread or cake to take back to your hotel, central Korat has several long-running bakeries and fresh-bake shops. Many open early, and the best-sellers tend to go fast.

items.name: Srifa Bakery, Korat branch
items.blurb: A legendary Isan bakery with filled breads, cookies and cakes at friendly prices — perfect to grab as a gift to bring home.

items.name: Chicky Bakery & Cafe
items.blurb: A custom-cake shop with a storefront selling cake slices and coffee, near the central stadium. Good for ordering a birthday cake or grabbing a small slice to snack on.

items.name: To Kiss Homemade Cake
items.blurb: A homemade cake shop in the Sueb Siri area, baking fresh every day with a focus on cake slices and pastries. Good for anyone who prefers a not-too-sweet flavour.

blocks.text: A one-day dessert crawl around the city

blocks.html: If you've got half a day to a full day and want to tick off several dessert spots, try this route. It works from the old town outward toward the water park — the distances are short, and you can hop between them easily by car or Grab.

items.activity: Open with Faifo Oldtown Cafe on Chumphon Road
items.note: Order the matcha croissant with coffee and shoot the old-shophouse corners before it gets busy.

items.activity: Stop by La-Moon Cafe on Suranari Road
items.note: A leafy cafe to sit and catch the breeze — order the fresh-milk green tea and a small slice of cheesecake.

items.activity: Grab a light lunch, then move on to KASEM Coffee on Det Udom Road
items.note: Go for the banana cake or burnt cheesecake and linger over a coffee.

items.activity: Head to Rosie.nak on Chomsurangyat Road
items.note: Unmissable for matcha fans — the matcha banoffee and a strong green-tea drink.

blocks.label: Evening
blocks.title: Wind down by the water park

items.activity: Finish at Na Bueng Coffee by Bueng Ta Lua water park
items.note: Order the Basque cheesecake, catch the breeze and watch the sunset before heading back.

items.activity: Pick up bread from Srifa Bakery to take back to the hotel
items.note: For late-night cravings, and a gift to bring home.

items: Most places are in the old town but spread across different roads. Without your own car, it's easier to Grab between them than to walk.
Signature items sell out fast. Popular homemade cakes and bingsu are usually made in limited batches — go late and you may miss out, so aim for the early afternoon.
Weekends get crowded. The well-known cafes have long queues on Saturday and Sunday. For a relaxed sit, go on a weekday or right at opening.
Check opening hours before you head out. Some shops close on Mondays or shift their hours by season — call or check the shop's page first to be sure.

faq.q: Which dessert cafe in central Korat is best?
faq.a: If you're into bingsu and cakes, go to De Forest Cafe & Bakery on Mittraphap Road. Matcha fans should head to Rosie.nak on Chomsurangyat Road. For an old-shophouse vibe with photogenic corners, try Faifo Oldtown Cafe on Chumphon Road. All three are in the old town and easy to reach.

faq.q: Where can I get Basque cheesecake in Korat?
faq.a: Na Bueng Coffee by Bueng Ta Lua water park makes the Basque cheesecake and blueberry cheesecake people mention most. The setting beside the park is relaxed, it opens roughly 09:00–18:30, and desserts start at around 50 THB.

faq.q: How much do cafe desserts cost in Korat?
faq.a: Drinks are mostly around 60–150 THB, while cakes and bingsu run roughly 70–350 THB per piece depending on the shop and size. Thai sweets and takeaway bakery items are cheaper, starting in the tens of baht.

faq.q: Where can I buy sweets as a gift to take home?
faq.a: Srifa Bakery (Korat branch) on Mukmontri Road is a long-established bakery that locals like to buy from for gifts, with filled breads, cookies and cakes. For traditional Thai sweets, look to Baan Khanom Thai in the Soi Chan area.

faq.q: Do dessert shops in Korat stay open late?
faq.a: Most cafes close around 18:00–19:00, but the city has some dessert and cold-sweet shops that stay open into the evening around the commercial districts. If you want a late-night sweet fix, check that particular shop's hours first.
